subject: Private deployment addendum — operator delegation & evidence requirements
messages:
From: Ryan Park <ryan.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Mills <sara.mills@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment addendum — operator scope & audit evidence

Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has asked us to surface the exact operator access and evidence model for the proposed VPC/on-prem addendum before the next legal review (next Wednesday). Two quick asks from our side:

- Can you confirm what operator actions Redwood would need for normal maintenance vs. emergency troubleshooting? We need a clear separation for our security review.
- We also need a short list of artifacts you can produce in support of an escrow-like request: snapshots, hashes, notarized checksums, evidence of successful restores, and a proposed cadence for deliveries.

I've attached our security questionnaire with the specific fields they flagged. Procurement has a tight window; can you confirm a MLP for evidence delivery and whether you will accept attestation in lieu of witnessed snapshots?

Thanks,
Ryan Park
Director, IT Security
Greenfield Health

Attachment: GF_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ryan Park <ryan.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — operator scope & audit evidence

Ryan — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the questionnaire. Looping in David (legal) and Grace (customer success / runbook owner) so we can provide a consolidated response. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a draft addendum and an internal MAP for signoff.

Quick answers:
- Operator actions: normal maintenance (software patching, metrics/health checks, config tweaks) will be limited to non-destructive operations and performed by named operator roles with RBAC. Emergency troubleshooting (hotfixes, critical rollback) requires pre-approved escalation and will be logged and timeboxed.
- Evidence artifacts: we can provide time-stamped encrypted snapshots, SHA-256 checksums, and restore logs. For customers that require higher assurance we offer a witness option (third-party verifier) or a notarized checksum bundle. We can accept a signed attestation for lower-risk customers as a compromise.

Grace will prepare the runbook excerpt and snapshot cadence. David, can you review scope language David — key questions: permitted operator actions, temporary console access windows, and whether an attestation-only route is acceptable to Legal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share MSA addendum draft with explicit operator-role bullets (by EOD tomorrow).
2) Customer to confirm whether they require witnessed snapshots or attestation.
3) If witnessed, propose scheduling a short validation window; if attestation, we’ll provide sample attestation language + sample snapshot.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ryan Park <ryan.park@greenfieldhealth.com>, Sara Mills <sara.mills@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — operator scope & audit evidence

Team / Ryan,

I reviewed the questionnaire and sketched a short MSA addendum draft (attached). Main legal positions we should propose:

- Operator access: narrow to named operator roles, explicit list of actions permitted. Add requirement for pre-approval of any destructive action and 24-hour notice where feasible.
- Temporary console access: allow time-boxed access (recommended 4 hours per incident) escrowed to a specific support engineer; access revocable by customer at any time.
- Evidence / escrow-like remedy: we will provide encrypted snapshot exports with SHA-256 checksums and signed attestation of snapshot integrity. For customers insisting on a custody transfer we propose a witnessless deposit model with an independent hash repository (Redwood uploads a signed checksum to a neutral repository) and a documented restore test run.
- Audit window: define a quarterly audit window and an on-demand audit process subject to 30-day notice (with a maximum of 2 ad-hoc audits per 12 months unless mutually agreed).

I attached the initial addendum (MSA_Addendum_DRAFT_v1.docx). If Greenfield insists on operator key handover or full escrow custody, expect more significant legal redlines (liability, IP residency, and indemnity clauses). Proposing we offer two paths in the addendum: "Attestation + scheduled restore validation" vs "Witnessed deposit + forensic restore test".

David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_Addendum_DRAFT_v1.docx (stub)

From: Ryan Park <ryan.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Mills <sara.mills@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — operator scope & audit evidence

David, Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround and draft. A couple of counterpoints from our procurement / security team after an internal review:

- Quarterly audit windows are fine for routine checks, but our compliance team wants one guaranteed on-demand audit per year without a 30-day notice (we accept narrow scope and pre-agreed checklist).
- We prefer custody of encryption keys for snapshots where possible; if Redwood cannot hand over keys, we need a stronger chain of custody for snapshot delivery (e.g., notarized checksum or third-party witness).
- Temporary console access should have stricter guardrails — multi-factor and session recording retained for at least 90 days.

We can accept either path you proposed but prefer the "Witnessed deposit + forensic restore test" for this deployment given the regulated data. Procurement attached the timeline and asks whether the witness option will add ~2–3 weeks to delivery.

Ryan

Attachment: Procurement_Timeline.xlsx (stub)

Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — operator scope & audit evidence

Ryan / Sara — appreciate the clarity. Proposed compromise below to keep procurement on track while meeting your compliance needs:

- Custody model: offer witnessed deposit path by default for this account (Greenfield can choose witnessed deposit). Witness process adds approximately 10 business days for scheduling + verification. If you select attestation-only later, we will provide a signed notarized checksum bundle and a recorded restore run.
- Audit rights: make one on-demand limited-scope audit per year without a 30-day notice; additional ad-hoc audits remain subject to 30-day notice. We'll include a pre-agreed checklist to limit scope (exported artifacts + restore logs).
- Console access & session recording: temporary access will require MFA, role-based session recording, and logs retained for 90 days. Access will be limited to a named operator and time-boxed (4-hour windows for troubleshooting, extendable by written agreement).

Next steps:
1) I'll attach a short Mutual Action Plan and the addendum language (see attachments).
2) If Greenfield confirms witnessed deposit, Grace will coordinate a single scheduled validation run (we'll propose 3 candidate dates).
3) Finalize addendum and route to DocuSign.

If this sounds reasonable, Sara / Ryan — confirm witnessed vs attestation and preferred date window for the validation run.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan.md (stub)
